chapter_theme: A single song under the heading Seyur (சேயூர்): the poet asks whether he must perish in the beds of women who bewitch all with their eyes, and praises the vel that turned his two deeds to dust.

721.reading: The poet describes the women with cloud-dark hair, bow brows, carp eyes, pearl smiles, breasts like towers, thread waists and peacock grace, who bewitch everyone with whirling glances, and asks whether he must perish in their beds. The praise names the vel thrown so that the gods' city cried out and the dark demons' army, the seven seas and the mountains were crushed, the son of the gracious Lady of the lotus and of the Lord the gods worship, Valli's bridegroom in a land of magizh, malati, rose-apple and jackfruit groves, and the lord of Valavapuri who threw the vel to turn his servant's two deeds to dust.
721.nuance: அடியேன் இருவினை தூள்பட அயில் ஏவிய: the vel that destroyed the demons is also said to have shattered the poet's own deeds, so the battle becomes his release. The song names the shrine வளவாபுரி, not Seyur.

source_issues: Song 721 is filed under சேயூர் but names its shrine வளவாபுரி; whether these are the same place should be checked.
